key_insight: A coronary calcium deep-learning model trained without any target-domain CTAC labels, using synthetic ungated scans from gated CT, outperformed expert calcium reading for risk stratification.
clinical_relevance: This approach could enable more reliable reporting of coronary artery calcium from routine attenuation-correction CT scans and improve identification of patients at risk for death or myocardial infarction.
method: Trained on expert-labeled high-quality gated CT, transferred to synthetic ungated images derived from the same scans.
Used cross-domain knowledge adaptation (KAD-CAC) without annotating or using real CTAC images during training.
Externally tested across two additional centers and compared with other DL models and expert reading.
evidence_signal: In 5,969 external patients, KAD-CAC showed higher agreement than comparator DL models and improved net reclassification for death or MI beyond clinical/perfusion baselines and expert CAC reading.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated retrospectively and may still depend on scanner, site, and workflow differences before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Deep Learning Trained Without Target-Domain Labels Improves Risk Stratification Over Expert Coronary Calcium Reading on Routine Attenuation Correction CT
